claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 9 years old and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Your son Alex is 9 years old and lives with you - that's helpful to know.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We're based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you! You live in the UK with Alex in Manchester.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and upkeep? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other daily needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm his parent and I provide for all his needs - his food, clothes, school things, everything really. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One more important question:

**Has Alex spent any extended time in hospital, care, or living with someone else recently? Or is he staying with you at home as usual?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's been staying with me at home as usual - just normal life really. He goes to school and comes home every day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for providing all that information.

Based on what you've told me, let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex:

- Alex is 9 years old (under 16)
- He lives with you in the UK (Manchester)
- You are responsible for his care and provide for all his needs
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He lives with you full-time and hasn't been in hospital or care

This means you meet all the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. Let me provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You live in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex and he lives with you full-time
- You provide for all his needs
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can go ahead and apply for Child Benefit. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you can still claim the benefit.

If you'd like to proceed with your application, you can make a claim through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
